method: Temporary phase and outermost lock probes, plus outermost cold bytecode compilation subphases. Thread and process CPU clocks separate CPU from wall time. Nested lock and compile holds are not added twice. Single-process full bin/ut at workers1,32,32,1. Default arena/GC, GC profiling enabled. Probe costs are not bounded; use uninstrumented cache-comparison runs for wall-time claims.
conclusions: In the first two 32-worker runs the compiler lock was held for 8.699 and 9.014 seconds in worker phases lasting 9.989 and 10.462 seconds. Startup prewarm is separate (~3.4-3.8 seconds).
Cold bytecode body walk dominates. Final processing is only~0.049 seconds in the detailed 32-worker run; moving only that host work cannot materially improve the suite.
Duplicate C root parses cost~0.03 seconds each. A fixture cache eliminating two parses would save only~0.06 seconds of CPU. No new cache is justified by this evidence.

The six nested-project root parses cost~0.13-0.16 seconds each and the four image-source root parses~0.17-0.23 seconds each. Further investigation is needed to separate necessary semantic work from redundant scanning.
followup: Root file lookup normalization was reduced without a new cache. See ut-parallel-path-lookup-results.json for before/after runs. All probes were removed before those measurements.
